title: Ordinary tensor is complete on a common projective chart
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $W,T$ be schemes and $f:T\to W$ any morphism [def-pc-scheme]. Assume $T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $\ell$ is a unit in every residue field of $T$ [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Write $B_S=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,S}$ for the completed coefficient sheaf on the small pro-etale site of a scheme $S$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $M,N\in D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},B_W)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $P,Q$ be bounded cochain complexes of $B_T$-module sheaves [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], each of whose terms is a sheaf-linear retract of a finite sum of copies of $B_T$. Suppose there are isomorphisms $Lf^*M\simeq [P]$ and $Lf^*N\simeq [Q]$, where the ordinary uncompleted pullback uses the canonical completed coefficient map [def-sf-ordinary-integral-derived-pullback, def-fix-qcqs-completion-ordinary-models]. Then $Lf^*(M\otimes^L_{B_W}N)$ is derived complete in the specified augmented Roos-triangle sense [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-weil-derived-complete]. The ordinary tensor is the one in the recorded IntegralOnSlice.duality model. No constructibility or completeness hypothesis is imposed on $M,N$.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.5, pp. 49–50, finite-projective local tensor step; Stacks sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A4 and Tag 0941. This isolates the ordinary-pullback/model transport in step 2 of lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion.

proof.text: The ordinaryIntegralDerivedPull and IntegralOnSlice.ordinaryDerivedPull presentations use the same completed coefficient map: the direct maps have exactly the same finite quotient projections. The limit universal property identifies these maps. Uniqueness of left adjoints then identifies the module pullbacks, and uniqueness of their total left derived functors identifies the ordinary derived pullbacks. No completeness of either input is used.

Use the ordinary tensor models of IntegralOnSlice.duality on W and T in the canonical ringed-topos derived tensor pullback theorem. It identifies the ordinary pullback of M tensor N with the ordinary tensor of their ordinary pullbacks. The tensor representative squares, rather than an unspecified comparison, characterize this isomorphism. Apply the tensor functor to the two supplied model isomorphisms to identify this tensor with the ordinary tensor of Q(P) and Q(Q).

Apply the bounded-projective tensor theorem to P and Q, using their support intervals and the specified sheaf-linear finite-free retracts. Their terms are flat, both complexes and their signed total tensor are K-flat, and the canonical completion unit is invertible on the localization of that total tensor. The duality model representative comparison identifies this localization with the ordinary tensor of Q(P) and Q(Q). Naturality transports unit invertibility along the composite of the representative and pullback comparison isomorphisms.

Apply the canonical completion-unit criterion on T: invertibility of this specified unit is equivalent to the Roos-triangle completeness predicate in the conclusion. This also treats empty T, rank-zero retracts, and zero complexes; no nonemptiness is imposed.

theorem projectiveTensorChartComplete
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    {W T : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace T] [QuasiSeparatedSpace T]
    (f : T ⟶ W) (hl : ∀ x : T, IsUnit (l : T.residueField x))
    (M N : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l E W))
    (P Q : CochainComplex (scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l E T) ℤ)
    (hP : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ k : ℤ, k < a ∨ b < k → IsZero (P.X k))
    (hQ : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ k : ℤ, k < a ∨ b < k → IsZero (Q.X k))
    (pP : ∀ k : ℤ, ∃ r : ℕ,
      ∃ i : P.X k ⟶ ∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin r ↦ SheafOfModules.unit
        (IntegralOnSlice.rings l E T none)),
      ∃ p : (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin r ↦ SheafOfModules.unit
        (IntegralOnSlice.rings l E T none))) ⟶ P.X k, i ≫ p = 𝟙 _)
    (pQ : ∀ k : ℤ, ∃ r : ℕ,
      ∃ i : Q.X k ⟶ ∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin r ↦ SheafOfModules.unit
        (IntegralOnSlice.rings l E T none)),
      ∃ p : (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin r ↦ SheafOfModules.unit
        (IntegralOnSlice.rings l E T none))) ⟶ Q.X k, i ≫ p = 𝟙 _)
    (eP : Nonempty ((ordinaryIntegralDerivedPull l E f).obj M ≅
      (@DerivedCategory.Q _ _ _ (scalarReductionSourceDerived.{u, u} l E T)).obj P))
    (eQ : Nonempty ((ordinaryIntegralDerivedPull l E f).obj N ≅
      (@DerivedCategory.Q _ _ _ (scalarReductionSourceDerived.{u, u} l E T)).obj Q)) :
    IntegralOnSlice.IsComplete l E T none
      ((IntegralOnSlice.ordinaryDerivedPull.{u, u} l E f).obj
        (((IntegralOnSlice.duality.{u, u} l E W none).closed.tensor).obj (M, N)))
